Actually subject_type is class of subject: "video game". But subject_type should be type of subject entity, e.g., "video game". So both subject_type and object_type? For instance of, object_type is "class". We'll set object_type "class". But guidelines: object_type is class the object is an instance of. For "video game" as object, it's a class. So object_type: "class". Subject_type: "video game". Might be redundant but okay.

Alternative title: relation "also known as" or "title in PAL territories". Use relation "title in region". Could use "title used in" with qualifier region. Simpler: relation "alternative title" object "Unirally". qualifiers: region PAL territories. So triplet: subject Uniracers, relation "alternative title", object "Unirally". qualifier: relation "region", object "PAL territories", object_type "region". subject_type "video game". object_type "video game title"? maybe "title". We'll set object_type "title".

Creators: relation "developer" or "created by". Use "developer" for DMA Design and Nintendo of America. Could have two separate triplets.

Platform: relation "platform", object "Super Nintendo Entertainment System". object_type "video game console". qualifier maybe region? Not needed.

Release dates: two separate triplets: subject Uniracers, relation "release date", object "December 1994". qualifier region "North America". Another: object "April 27 1995". qualifier region "PAL territories". object_type date.

Also maybe "release region" but we can use qualifier.
